# opsward

Diagnose, generate, and maintain the AI agent setup of your projects —
CLAUDE.md, skills, subagents, rules, and supporting docs.

Opsward works in two modes:

- **CLI mode** — deterministic, pure-code analysis you run directly. No AI involved.
- **Claude Code mode** — install opsward as Claude Code skills so that Claude runs the
  CLI tools, interprets results intelligently, and acts on suggestions. No API keys
  needed — Claude Code is the AI engine.

## Install

```bash
pip install opsward
```

---

## CLI Mode (no AI)

These commands are deterministic Python code — regex scoring, filesystem checks,
template substitution. Same input always gives the same output.

### Diagnose

Score your project’s AI setup health:

```bash
opsward diagnose .
```

```default
Diagnosis Report: myproject
Project type: python
Overall score: 72/100  (Grade: C)

Components:
  CLAUDE.md quality         [################....] 81/100
  Documentation             [##############......] 70/100
  Skills                    [############........] 60/100
  Setup (rules/agents/hooks) [##########..........] 50/100
  Cross-references          [####################] 100/100

Missing:
  [ ] docs_guide.md
  [ ] docs/known_issues.md

Suggestions:
  1. Create a docs_guide.md to index your documentation
  2. Consider adding hooks in .claude/hooks.json
```

### Generate

Create missing artifacts (dry run by default):

```bash
opsward generate .
opsward generate . --write   # actually create files
```

Generates CLAUDE.md, docs (architecture, conventions, known_issues, etc.),
skill templates, and agents — only what’s missing, never overwrites existing files.

### Maintain

Find stale references and drift:

```bash
opsward maintain .
```

```default
myproject: 3 issue(s)

  [stale_path → align] CLAUDE.md references `src/old_module.py` but it does not exist
  [sync_issue → align] `new_doc.md` exists in docs/ but is not listed in docs_guide.md
  [empty_doc → align] `conventions.md` appears to be an empty stub (12 bytes)
```

Each finding carries a recommended triage: **align** (the code is right, update the config), **revert** (the config is right, restore the code) or **ignore** (the reference is legitimately volatile). To ignore one, put `<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->` at the end of its line, or alone on the line before it; every path check (stale paths, the currency score, cross-references, ADR drift) then skips it.

**Config changelog** (opt-in): create `config_changelog.md` in the docs folder and give every change to the agent config (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, `.claude/`) one dated line, newest first, saying what changed and why, e.g. `- 2026-10-20: moved the CLI-golden procedure out of CLAUDE.md (over budget); align`. Once the file exists, `opsward maintain` reports a `config_changelog` finding whenever a config commit is newer than the last changelog commit.

### Fleet

Diagnose many repos at once and roll the results up (grades, what is missing where, the weakest components, the worst repos):

```bash
opsward fleet ~/proj/a ~/proj/b            # explicit roots
opsward fleet --under ~/proj --depth 2     # every git repo under a folder
opsward fleet --under ~/proj --manifest ~/.local/share/opsward/fleet.json
opsward fleet --manifest ~/.local/share/opsward/fleet.json   # re-run the remembered fleet
```

`--manifest` remembers the fleet: it writes the roots and the latest name-keyed summary to that JSON file. The roots are this machine’s paths, so keep the manifest out of version control (opsward warns when it sits in a git work tree unignored).

### Output Formats

All CLI commands support `--format json` for machine-parseable output:

```bash
opsward diagnose . --format json
opsward generate . --format json
opsward maintain . --format json
```

---

## Claude Code Mode (AI-enhanced)

Install opsward’s skills into Claude Code, and Claude becomes an intelligent
layer on top of the deterministic tools. It doesn’t just run opsward — it goes
beyond the heuristic scores by reading actual source code, reasoning about
accuracy, and making intelligent edits.

### Install Skills

```bash
opsward install-skills --write                    # into ./.claude/ (project-level)
opsward install-skills --global-install --write   # into ~/.claude/ (all projects)
```

### What the Skills Do

Once installed, these skills activate automatically in Claude Code when you ask
the right thing:

| Skill              | Trigger                     | What it does                                                                           |
|--------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `opsward`          | “check my setup”, “opsward” | Diagnose → decide next step → generate or maintain → re-diagnose                       |
| `opsward-diagnose` | “audit my AI config”        | Run `opsward diagnose`, then read code to assess semantic quality, offer fixes         |
| `opsward-generate` | “scaffold AI setup”         | Run `opsward generate`, then read the codebase and replace templates with real content |
| `opsward-maintain` | “check for staleness”       | Run `opsward maintain`, then check for semantic drift (docs that no longer match code) |

### How It Works

1. **Opsward CLI** runs deterministic checks (regex scoring, path validation, template substitution) — fast, reproducible, no AI
2. **Claude reads the output** and adds deeper analysis: reads actual source code, checks if docs match reality, verifies commands are correct
3. **Claude proposes fixes** — not just what opsward suggests, but what it discovers by understanding the code
4. **Claude applies fixes** with user approval, then re-runs opsward to show improvement

The CLI provides the structural analysis. Claude provides the semantic understanding and action.

### Permissions

The skills use Claude Code’s standard permission model — no special permissions are
assumed or required:

- **Read-only operations** (reading files, searching code, running `opsward diagnose`): always safe, used freely
- **Write operations** (creating docs, editing CLAUDE.md): Claude Code prompts the user for each action per their permission settings
- **Destructive operations** (deleting files, removing content): always ask for explicit confirmation

If you want faster workflows (e.g., auto-approve file creation during generation),
you can configure that in your Claude Code permission settings — but opsward skills
never assume it.

---

## What It Checks

**CLAUDE.md quality** (6 dimensions):

- Commands & workflows — are build/test/lint commands documented?
- Architecture clarity — is there a module map with role descriptions?
- Conventions — are project-specific style rules present?
- Conciseness — is the file scannable, not bloated?
- Currency — do referenced paths actually exist?
- Actionability — are instructions specific enough to act on?

**Documentation completeness**: docs_guide.md, architecture.md, conventions.md,
known_issues.md, and content quality.

**Skills & agents**: SKILL.md presence, descriptions, setup-auditor agent.

**Cross-references**: paths in CLAUDE.md validated against the filesystem.

**Overall health**: weighted score (A–F grade) combining all components.

**Security advisories** (reported, never scored; modelled on the OWASP Top 10 for agentic applications): unrestricted Bash in a skill’s `allowed-tools` or in `permissions.allow`, `bypassPermissions`, a download piped into a shell, `eval` of a built string, unpinned `npx`/`uvx` packages in hooks and MCP servers, text that tries to override the agent’s other instructions, and committed credentials. They are heuristics, so they never move the grade or fail `--min-score`.

## Python API

```python
from pathlib import Path
from opsward import scan, diagnose, generate, generate_skills, maintain
from opsward import recommend_skills, validate_skill_spec

sr = scan(".")
report = diagnose(sr)
print(report)  # human-readable report card
print(report.grade)  # 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D', or 'F'

files = generate(sr)  # list[GeneratedFile]
issues = maintain(sr)  # list[MaintenanceSuggestion]

# Recommend ecosystem skills based on tech stack
recs = recommend_skills(sr)  # list[SkillRecommendation]

# Validate skills against agentskills.io spec
for skill in sr.skills:
    violations = validate_skill_spec(skill)

# Install skills programmatically
skill_files = generate_skills(Path.home() / ".claude")
```

### Evals (opt-in, report-only)

The rubric scores form; evals ask whether a config actually helps. They make model calls, so they never gate and never run by default:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from opsward.evals import (
    judge_claude_md,
    anthropic_judge,
    run_golden_tasks,
    GoldenTask,
    anthropic_agent,
)

# LLM-as-judge for the subjective dimensions (actionability, conciseness), next to the rubric's score
print(
    judge_claude_md(Path("CLAUDE.md").read_text(), judge=anthropic_judge(), samples=3)
)

# Golden tasks: does the agent honour a convention with the config, and not without it?
tasks = [GoldenTask("kw-only", "Write a function f(a, b, c).", expect=[r"\*,"])]
print(
    run_golden_tasks(
        tasks, agent=anthropic_agent(), config=Path("CLAUDE.md").read_text(), runs=3
    )
)
```

`pip install 'opsward[eval]'` for the paid judge and agent. Without them, `judge_claude_md` defaults to `rubric_judge` (opsward’s own rubric, free) and `echo_agent` exercises the golden-task harness without a model.

From the shell, `opsward eval` runs both and exits 0 whenever it ran (a report, never a gate; 2 on a usage error). It finds a repo’s golden tasks at `<docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json` (`misc/docs/` for Python, `docs/` for JS/TS) unless `--tasks` names a file:

```bash
opsward eval .                                   # free: the rubric judge and the echo agent
opsward eval . --judge anthropic --samples 3     # paid model calls (pip install 'opsward[eval]')
opsward eval . --tasks evals.json --runs 5 --format json
```

## CI Integration

Use opsward in CI to enforce AI setup quality:

```bash
# Fail if overall score drops below 60
opsward diagnose . --min-score 60

# Machine-parseable output for CI tooling
opsward diagnose . --format json --min-score 60
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ai-setup-check.yml
name: AI Setup Check
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install opsward
      - run: opsward diagnose . --min-score 60
```

Two gates, for two jobs: `diagnose --min-score` is the cheap scored gate, and `lint` is the strict one, pass or fail with no score. `lint` checks every project skill against the agentskills.io spec and the hooks config for shapes Claude Code silently ignores, and exits 1 on any finding:

```bash
opsward lint .                          # opsward's own spec check, plus skill.validate() when installed
opsward lint . --validators opsward     # only opsward's check
pip install 'opsward[lint]'             # adds the `skill` package's validate()
# external linters, opt-in by name (opsward does not install them; `auto` never runs them):
npm install -g agnix                    # --validators agnix
pip install skillcheck                  # --validators skillcheck
```

The repo ships a reusable GitHub Action and pre-commit hooks:

```yaml
# a workflow step, after actions/checkout
- uses: thorwhalen/opsward@<a release tag>
  with:
    min-score: "70"   # "" skips the scored gate
    lint: "true"
```

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
- repo: https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward
  rev: <a release tag>
  hooks:
    - id: opsward-lint
    - id: opsward-diagnose
      args: [--min-score, "70"]
```

### opsward.cli.diagnose(\*project_roots, format='text', verbose=False, min_score=80)

Diagnose the AI agent setup of one or more projects.

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – one or more paths to project directories
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’
  * **verbose** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – show additional detail in text output
  * **min_score** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – minimum overall score to pass (exit 0); below this exits 1

### opsward.cli.eval_(project_root, , judge='rubric', samples=1, tasks='', runs=1, format='text')

Report-only evals of a project’s agent setup: an LLM judge of CLAUDE.md, and golden tasks.

The judge scores CLAUDE.md’s subjective dimensions next to the rubric’s own score. The
golden tasks (a JSON list of {name, prompt, expect, forbid}, by default
<docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json) run with and without CLAUDE.md and report the pass-rate
delta. –judge rubric is free and deterministic (the rubric judge and an agent that
quotes the config: it checks the harness, not a model); –judge anthropic makes paid
calls (pip install ‘opsward[eval]’). Exits 0 whenever it ran (a report, never a gate);
2 only on a usage error.

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the project directory
  * **judge** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – ‘rubric’ (free) or ‘anthropic’ (paid model calls)
  * **samples** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – judge samples per dimension (the median is reported)
  * **tasks** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – golden-tasks JSON file (default: <docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json, if present)
  * **runs** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – runs per golden task and arm
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’

### opsward.cli.find(query, \*project_roots, kinds='skill,agent', semantic=False, limit=10)

Find assets (skills, agents, docs) across one or more projects by QUERY.

Cross-repo asset discovery via the toolery package
(install with: pip install ‘opsward[discovery]’).

* **Parameters:**
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – search query
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – one or more project directories (default: current dir)
  * **kinds** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – comma-separated asset kinds — skill, agent, doc
  * **semantic** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – use toolery’s ir semantic backend (needs toolery[ir])
  * **limit** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – max results to show

### opsward.cli.fleet(\*project_roots, under='', depth=1, format='text', manifest='')

Diagnose many projects at once and roll the results up into one fleet report.

The fleet is the given roots, plus the git repos found under –under. With –manifest
the fleet is remembered: the roots and the latest summary are written to that JSON
file, and a later run with only –manifest re-diagnoses the same roots (given roots or
–under replace them). The manifest holds this machine’s absolute paths, so keep it
out of version control. Exits 1 when any root could not be diagnosed.

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – project directories to diagnose
  * **under** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – also diagnose every git repo found under this directory
  * **depth** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – how many levels below –under to look for git repos
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’ (the name-keyed summary)
  * **manifest** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – JSON file that remembers the fleet’s roots and its latest summary

### opsward.cli.generate(\*project_roots, write=False, format='text', agents_md=False, hooks=False)

Generate missing AI setup artifacts for one or more projects.

By default, shows what would be created (dry run). Use –write to

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – one or more paths to project directories
  * **write** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – actually write files (default: dry run)
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’
  * **agents_md** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – also generate AGENTS.md (cross-platform agent instructions)
  * **hooks** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – also generate starter hook scripts

  * **write** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – actually write files (default: dry run)

### opsward.cli.lint(\*project_roots, validators='auto', format='text')

Check skill specs and the hooks config: pass or fail, no score (exit 1 on any finding).

The strict counterpart of `diagnose --min-score`, for CI and pre-commit. Validators:
opsward (its own agentskills.io check, always there), skill (the skill package’s
validate(); pip install ‘opsward[lint]’), and the external agnix and skillcheck
linters (opt-in by name). auto runs opsward and skill, each when installed.

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – one or more project directories (default: current dir)
  * **validators** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – ‘auto’, or a comma list of: opsward, skill, agnix, skillcheck
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’

### opsward.cli.maintain(\*project_roots, format='text')

Check for stale references, out-of-sync docs, and other drift.

Each finding carries a recommended triage: align (update the config to match the
code), revert (restore the code the config describes) or ignore (a legitimately
volatile reference: put `opsward: ignore-path` on its line).

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – one or more paths to project directories
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’

### opsward.cli.new(title, write=False, project_root='.', status='Proposed', evidence='')

Allocate the next numbered ADR for TITLE (dry run unless –write; never overwrites).

* **Parameters:**
  * **title** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the decision’s title; the file name is derived from it
  * **write** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – actually write the file (default: dry run)
  * **project_root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the project directory (default: current dir)
  * **status** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – initial status — Proposed (default), or Accepted when the human has accepted it
  * **evidence** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the issue, discussion or PR this rests on (a URL or #N)

### opsward.cli.note(text, write=False, project_root='.')

Append TEXT as a dated one-line decision (a Y-statement) to decisions/log.md (dry run unless –write).

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the decision: “In the context of …, facing …, we decided for …, because …”
  * **write** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – actually append (default: dry run); the log is created from its template when missing
  * **project_root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the project directory (default: current dir)

### opsward.cli.recommend(\*project_roots, format='text')

Recommend ecosystem skills based on the project’s tech stack.

Analyzes dependencies and suggests skills from the community catalog.

* **Parameters:**
  * **project_roots** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – one or more paths to project directories
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – output format — ‘text’ or ‘json’


# _autosummary/opsward.data.html.md

# opsward.data

Bundled package resources for opsward, accessed via `importlib.resources.files("opsward.data")`.

Holds the generation templates (under `templates/`) and any other static
assets the generator installs into target projects. Never hardcode filesystem
paths to these resources – resolve them through `importlib.resources`.

| [`templates`](_autosummary/opsward.data.templates.html.md#module-opsward.data.templates)   | Generation templates organized by target project type.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|


# _autosummary/opsward.data.templates.html.md

# opsward.data.templates

Generation templates organized by target project type.

`shared/` holds templates (and installable Claude Code skills) that apply to
any project; `python/` and `jsts/` hold language-specific variants. The
generator reads these via `importlib.resources` and substitutes
`${variable}` placeholders (`string.Template`) before writing to a target.


# _autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md

# opsward.decisions

Decision capture: numbered ADRs, the one-line decision log, and their drift.

Two tiers, per ADR 0010 and `misc/docs/research/adr_and_home_finding.md`: a
trivial or medium decision is one **Y-statement** line appended to `decisions/log.md`
(“In the context of …, facing …, we decided for …, to achieve …, accepting …,
because …”); a load-bearing, expensive-to-reverse one is a numbered **MADR** file
`decisions/NNNN-slug.md` that is never edited once accepted, only superseded.

Pure functions here; the CLI (`opsward decision new|note`) is the only writer, and
it never overwrites. `maintain` uses [`check_decisions()`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.check_decisions) to report an ADR that
cites a path which no longer exists, or that has no Status, which is how rot shows up.

### Functions

| [`adr_files`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.adr_files)(decisions_dir)                         | The numbered ADR files in *decisions_dir*, in number order (the template is not one).                                                                   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_decisions`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.check_decisions)(sr)                              | `maintain` check: ADRs citing paths that no longer exist, or carrying no status.                                                                        |
| [`cited_paths`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.cited_paths)(content)                             | Paths an ADR cites as current, outside fenced code: bare path tokens and Markdown link targets (relative ones only; URLs and host names are not paths). |
| [`clean_title`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.clean_title)(title)                               | One line, single-spaced; empty is an error the CLI reports.                                                                                             |
| [`decision_docs`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.decision_docs)(sr)                                | The ADRs a scan found (`ScanResult.decisions`), numbered files only.                                                                                    |
| [`log_append`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.log_append)(decisions_dir, text, \*[, date])      | The log file and the full content it should hold after appending *text*.                                                                                |
| [`log_entry`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.log_entry)(text, \*[, date])                      | One Y-statement line for `decisions/log.md`.                                                                                                            |
| [`new_adr`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.new_adr)(decisions_dir, title, \*[, status, ...]) | The next numbered ADR for *title*, rendered from the `adr.md` template.                                                                                 |
| [`next_number`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.next_number)(decisions_dir)                       | One more than the highest numbered ADR, so numbers never collide (1 for an empty dir).                                                                  |
| [`slugify`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.slugify)(title)                                   | A file-name slug: lowercase, hyphens, nothing else, at most 60 characters.                                                                              |
| [`status_of`](_autosummary/opsward.decisions.html.md#opsward.decisions.status_of)(content)                               | The ADR's status text, from a `## Status` heading, a `**Status:**` line or MADR front matter; `None` when there is none.                                |

### opsward.decisions.adr_files(decisions_dir)

The numbered ADR files in *decisions_dir*, in number order (the template is not one).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

### opsward.decisions.check_decisions(sr)

`maintain` check: ADRs citing paths that no longer exist, or carrying no status.

Rot in a decision record is a path that moved: the rationale still reads well and
points at nothing. Superseded, deprecated and rejected ADRs are history and are not
checked for paths: the superseding record is where the current paths live. This
reports; it never rewrites an accepted ADR (ADR 0010).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`MaintenanceSuggestion`](_autosummary/opsward.base.html.md#opsward.base.MaintenanceSuggestion)]

### opsward.decisions.cited_paths(content)

Paths an ADR cites as current, outside fenced code: bare path tokens and Markdown
link targets (relative ones only; URLs and host names are not paths).

A path the record cites as history is not checked: wrap it in `~~strikethrough~~`,
or say so on the line (`formerly`, `previously`, `moved`, `migrated`,
`renamed`, `replaced`, `removed`, `retired`, `deleted`), as in “we moved `pkg/old.py` to `pkg/new.py`” — there
only `pkg/new.py` must exist.

```pycon
>>> cited_paths("See `pkg/a.py`, [0002](0002-x.md), [doc](../research/r.md), https://x.io/a/b.py, docs.github.com/en/x.md\n```\nsrc/in/fence.py\n```")
['../research/r.md', '0002-x.md', 'pkg/a.py']
>>> cited_paths("We moved `pkg/old.py` to `pkg/new.py`; ~~`pkg/gone.py`~~ is history.")
['pkg/new.py']
>>> cited_paths("It was read from `pkg/live.py`.\nRenamed [old](../old.md) to [new](../new.md).")
['../new.md', 'pkg/live.py']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### opsward.decisions.clean_title(title)

One line, single-spaced; empty is an error the CLI reports.

```pycon
>>> clean_title("  two\n lines ")
'two lines'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### opsward.decisions.decision_docs(sr)

The ADRs a scan found (`ScanResult.decisions`), numbered files only.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`DocSpec`](_autosummary/opsward.base.html.md#opsward.base.DocSpec)]

### opsward.decisions.log_append(decisions_dir, text, , date=None)

The log file and the full content it should hold after appending *text*.

A missing log starts from the `log.md` template. The existing log is read
strictly: an unreadable or non-UTF-8 log raises (`OSError` /
`UnicodeDecodeError`) rather than being replaced by the new line alone. The
caller writes; this does not.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### opsward.decisions.log_entry(text, , date=None)

One Y-statement line for `decisions/log.md`.

```pycon
>>> log_entry("In the context of goldens, facing drift, we decided for pinning.", date=_dt.date(2026, 10, 19))
'- 2026-10-19 — In the context of goldens, facing drift, we decided for pinning.'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### opsward.decisions.new_adr(decisions_dir, title, , status='Proposed', date=None, evidence='')

The next numbered ADR for *title*, rendered from the `adr.md` template.

*evidence* is the issue, discussion or PR the decision rests on (a URL or `#N`);
it lands in the Evidence section so the three surfaces stay linked.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> gf = new_adr(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()), "Pin the CLI surface", date=_dt.date(2026, 10, 19), evidence="#8")
>>> gf.target_path.name, gf.content.splitlines()[0]
('0001-pin-the-cli-surface.md', '# 0001 — Pin the CLI surface')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`GeneratedFile`](_autosummary/opsward.base.html.md#opsward.base.GeneratedFile)

One more than the highest numbered ADR, so numbers never collide (1 for an empty dir).

```pycon

>>> next_number(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()))
1
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### opsward.decisions.slugify(title)

A file-name slug: lowercase, hyphens, nothing else, at most 60 characters.

```pycon
>>> slugify("Pin the CLI surface by goldens!")
```

* **Return type:**

### opsward.decisions.status_of(content)

The ADR’s status text, from a `## Status` heading, a `**Status:**` line or

```pycon
>>> status_of("# x\n\n## Status\n\nAccepted (2026-01-01)\n")
'Accepted (2026-01-01)'
>>> status_of("---\nstatus: accepted\n---\n# x\n"), status_of("**Status:** Superseded by 0003"), status_of("# x\nno status")
('accepted', 'Superseded by 0003', None)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/opsward.discover.html.md

# opsward.discover

Optional cross-repo asset discovery, delegating to the `toolery` package.

opsward scans and *scores* the AI setup of one repo; this adds *finding* assets — skills,
subagents, docs — across one or more repos. It is opt-in and keeps opsward’s core
dependency-light: `pip install 'opsward[discovery]'` pulls in `toolery` (add
`toolery[ir]` for semantic search). Conceptually this is opsward’s per-repo/fleet
orchestration meeting toolery’s discovery engine (epic #12 → #13).

### Functions

| [`find_assets`](_autosummary/opsward.discover.html.md#opsward.discover.find_assets)(\*roots, query[, kinds, ...])   | Find assets matching `query` across one or more project `roots`.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### opsward.discover.find_assets(\*roots, query, kinds='skill,agent', semantic=False, limit=10)

Find assets matching `query` across one or more project `roots`.

Harvests the requested `kinds` (comma-separated string or a sequence of
`"skill"`/`"agent"`/`"doc"`) from each root via `toolery` and returns ranked
`(Card, score)` results. With `semantic=True`, uses `toolery`’s ir federated
backend (needs `toolery[ir]`). Defaults to the current directory when no roots given.


# _autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md

# opsward.evals

Eval harness (opsward#17, gap 3): opt-in, report-only quality signals beyond the rubric.

Two layers, both of which *report* and never gate (model calls cost money and are
nondeterministic, so the deterministic rubric stays the only gate):

* **LLM-as-judge** for the rubric’s subjective dimensions (actionability, conciseness):
  [`judge_claude_md()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.judge_claude_md) asks a *judge* to score CLAUDE.md against an explicit rubric,
  > `samples` times, and reports the median next to the rubric’s own score.
* **Golden tasks**: [`run_golden_tasks()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.run_golden_tasks) runs an *agent* on repo-specific tasks with
  and without a candidate config, and checks each output against the task’s `expect` /
  `forbid` patterns. The with-minus-without pass rate is the signal that a config helps.

The judge and the agent are injected. [`rubric_judge()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.rubric_judge) (the default judge) and
[`echo_agent()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.echo_agent) are free and deterministic – they exercise the harness and anchor the
scale – while [`anthropic_judge()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.anthropic_judge) and [`anthropic_agent()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.anthropic_agent) make paid calls through
the `anthropic` SDK (`pip install 'opsward[eval]'`) and are never used by default.

```pycon
>>> report = judge_claude_md("# P\n\n## Commands\n\n```bash\npytest\n```\n")
>>> sorted(report.scores), report.judge
(['actionability', 'conciseness'], 'rubric')
>>> tasks = [GoldenTask("kw", "Write f(a, b, c)", expect=[r"\*,"])]
>>> golden = run_golden_tasks(tasks, agent=echo_agent, config="Use `*,` before the 3rd arg.")
>>> golden.delta()
1.0
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_JUDGE_MODEL`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.DFLT_JUDGE_MODEL)          | Default model for the paid judge and agent; override with `model=`.                                                                         |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`JUDGE_RUBRICS`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.JUDGE_RUBRICS)             | vague "rate the quality" prompts give noise, anchored bands do not.                                                                         |
| [`Judge`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.Judge)                     | the JSON object above).                                                                                                                     |
| [`Agent`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.Agent)                     | An agent does a task under a config (CLAUDE.md text; `""` = no config) and returns its output.                                              |
| [`DFLT_GOLDEN_TASKS_RELPATH`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.DFLT_GOLDEN_TASKS_RELPATH) | Where a repo keeps its golden tasks, relative to its docs folder (`opsward.scan.docs_dir_for()`: `misc/docs` for Python, `docs` for JS/TS). |

### Functions

| [`anthropic_agent`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.anthropic_agent)(\*[, model, client, max_tokens])   | A paid single-call agent: the config is the system prompt, the task the user turn.                                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`anthropic_judge`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.anthropic_judge)(\*[, model, client, max_tokens])   | A paid judge over the Messages API.                                                                                             |
| [`echo_agent`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.echo_agent)(task, config)                           | The free agent: "does" the task by quoting its config, so a config that states the convention passes and an empty one does not. |
| [`golden_tasks_path`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.golden_tasks_path)(scan_result)                     | The default golden-tasks file of a scanned project (it may not exist).                                                          |
| [`judge_claude_md`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.judge_claude_md)(content, \*[, judge, ...])         | Score CLAUDE.md `content` on each subjective dimension, `samples` times each.                                                   |
| [`load_golden_tasks`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.load_golden_tasks)(path)                            | Tasks from a JSON list of `{"name", "prompt", "expect": [...], "forbid": [...]}`.                                               |
| [`parse_verdict`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.parse_verdict)(reply, \*, max_score)                | `(score, reasoning)` from a judge reply: the *last* JSON object in it with a `score`.                                           |

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

config), so a flaky agent cannot skew [`delta()`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.GoldenReport.delta); the errors are listed.

### opsward.evals.judge_claude_md(content, \*, judge=<function rubric_judge>, dimensions=('actionability', 'conciseness'), samples=1)

A reply that cannot be parsed is recorded as an error on its dimension, never raised.

* **Raises:**

### opsward.evals.parse_verdict(reply, , max_score)

`(score, reasoning)` from a judge reply: the *last* JSON object in it with a `score`.

The last, because a judge that quotes a snippet or restates the format writes its
verdict at the end. `9`, `9.0` and `"9"` are all read as 9.

* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – no JSON object with a `score`, or one that is not an integer in
  `0..max_score`.
* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> parse_verdict('Quote {"a": 1}. Verdict: {"reasoning": "ok", "score": 12}', max_score=15)
(12, 'ok')
```

### opsward.evals.rubric_judge(request)

The free, deterministic judge: answers with opsward’s own rubric score.

It exercises the harness end to end and anchors the scale (a real judge’s scores are
read next to it), but it is not an independent opinion.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### opsward.evals.run_golden_tasks(tasks, , agent, config, baseline='', runs=1)

Run every task `runs` times under `config` and under `baseline`; count passes.

An agent error is recorded, never raised, and leaves that run out of the pass rate.

* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – two tasks share a name, or `runs < 1`.
* **Return type:**
  [`GoldenReport`](_autosummary/opsward.evals.html.md#opsward.evals.GoldenReport)

# _autosummary/opsward.lint.html.md

# opsward.lint

Schema lint (opsward#17, gap 2): spec and config violations, pass or fail, no score.

`diagnose --min-score` is the cheap scored gate; `lint` is the strict one. It runs
every *validator* over every project skill, and checks the hooks config, and reports each
violation with a repo-relative path. A validator is `SkillInfo -> list[str]`:

* `opsward` – opsward’s own agentskills.io spec check (`validate_skill_spec()`),
  always available;
* `skill` – the `skill` package’s `skill.validate()` (`pip install 'opsward[lint]'`),
  which composes its own registered validators;
* `agnix` and `skillcheck` – external linters, run as subprocesses
  (`npm install -g agnix`, `pip install skillcheck`); their JSON diagnostics of level
  `error` and `warning` become findings. opsward does not depend on either, and they
  are opt-in by name: their rule sets are wider and noisier than the spec check, so a
  gate on `"auto"` must not turn red because a machine happens to have one installed.

`"auto"` (the default) is [`AUTO_VALIDATORS`](_autosummary/opsward.lint.html.md#opsward.lint.AUTO_VALIDATORS), each when it is available. A host
can pass any mapping of name to validator instead.

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from opsward.base import ScanResult, SkillInfo
>>> sr = ScanResult(Path("repo"), skills=[SkillInfo("Bad_Name", Path("repo/.claude/skills/Bad_Name"),
...                                                 has_skill_md=True, frontmatter={"name": "Bad_Name"})])
>>> findings = list(lint(sr, validators={"opsward": opsward_validator}))
>>> findings[0].path, findings[0].source
('.claude/skills/Bad_Name', 'opsward')
```

# _autosummary/opsward.portability.html.md

# opsward.portability

Multi-host portability: which agent hosts a repo satisfies, and canonical↔render drift.

The canonical project brief is `AGENTS.md` (opsward#15). Every other host’s instruction
file (`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, …) is a *render*
of it, related to it in one of three ways:

* `symlink` — the file is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`: byte-identical, cannot drift;
* `import` — the file imports it (`@AGENTS.md`) and adds host-only deltas: the
  recommended shape for hosts with an import syntax (Claude Code, Gemini CLI);
* `copy` — a separate file: everything in it can drift from the canonical.

The check is a *linter*: the canonical is authoritative and drift in a render is
reported, never merged back. Three finding kinds, matched section by section (by
normalised heading):

* `stale` — a canonical section is missing from a copy;
* `diverged` — a section is in both, with different bodies (a stale render or a hand
  edit in the render: the files alone cannot say which);
* `host_only` — a section only the render has: promote it to `AGENTS.md` if it is
  portable, or keep it as a host delta (after an `@AGENTS.md` import).

Scoped-rule folders (`.cursor/rules/`, `.windsurf/rules/`, `.clinerules/`) count
towards coverage but are not compared: they are not renders of one brief.

Files that are only coverage signals (`CONVENTIONS.md` is often a contributor doc, not a
render) are compared only when they import or link the canonical.

`read_host_files` is read-only (it backs `scan`); `analyze` is pure.

```pycon
>>> report = analyze(
...     "# P\n\n## Build\n\npytest\n",
...     {"CLAUDE.md": HostFile("CLAUDE.md", "## Build\n\npytest -x\n## Claude\n\nx\n")},
... )
>>> report.coverage["claude"], report.coverage["codex"]
('copy', 'native')
>>> sorted((f.kind, f.section) for f in report.findings)
[('diverged', 'build'), ('host_only', 'claude')]
```

### Functions

| [`analyze`](_autosummary/opsward.portability.html.md#opsward.portability.analyze)(canonical, host_files, \*[, hosts])   | Coverage and drift of *host_files* against the *canonical* `AGENTS.md` text.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_portability`](_autosummary/opsward.portability.html.md#opsward.portability.check_portability)(root, \*[, hosts])          | `analyze` over what is on disk under *root*: the library entry point.          |
| [`read_host_files`](_autosummary/opsward.portability.html.md#opsward.portability.read_host_files)(root, \*[, hosts])            | Every host instruction file and rule folder present under *root*.              |
| [`summarize`](_autosummary/opsward.portability.html.md#opsward.portability.summarize)(report)                             | One diagnose suggestion per drifting render.                                   |

# _autosummary/opsward.scan.html.md

# opsward.scan

### opsward.scan(project_root, \*, claude_config_dir=<object object>)

Scan *project_root* and return a ScanResult.

`claude_config_dir` is the user’s Claude Code config dir, whose `skills/` is
the global scope a project skill competes with (shadowing, listing budget). It
defaults to `default_claude_config_dir()`; pass `None` to read nothing
outside the project (tests, portable goldens). Reading it is still read-only.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> r = scan(pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()), claude_config_dir=None)
>>> r.project_type, r.global_skills
(<ProjectType.unknown: 'unknown'>, [])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`ScanResult`](_autosummary/opsward.base.html.md#opsward.base.ScanResult)

### opsward.score.skill_reachability_findings(sr, , suggestions, listing_budget_chars=30000)

Why a project skill may never trigger, as note lines (and one suggestion each).

Three shapes from the #23 report: a project skill **shadowed** by a global one of the
same name (Claude Code resolves personal > project, verified in a fresh session); an
**unmigrated bridge** (a real directory under `.claude/skills` while the repo also
holds the skill at its canonical location); and a **listing budget** that the global
scope plus this project’s skills cannot fit, so descriptions get dropped
least-invoked-first. The global scope comes from `ScanResult.global_skills`;
with none (`scan(..., claude_config_dir=None)`) only the bridge check runs.

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from opsward.base import ScanResult, SkillInfo
>>> g = SkillInfo(name='lint', path=Path('/g/lint'), has_skill_md=True, description='Global lint.', real_path=Path('/g/lint'))
>>> p = SkillInfo(name='lint', path=Path('/p/.claude/skills/lint'), has_skill_md=True, description='Project lint.', real_path=Path('/p/.claude/skills/lint'))
>>> sr = ScanResult(project_root=Path('/p'), skills=[p], global_skills=[g])
>>> s = []
>>> skill_reachability_findings(sr, suggestions=s)[0][:46]
'Skill "lint": shadowed by the global skill of '
>>> len(s)
1
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### opsward.score.validate_hooks_config(cfg)

Validate a hooks config against Claude Code’s expected shape.

Returns a list of human-readable violation strings (empty = valid). Catches
the silent-failure traps: a non-string `matcher`, an unknown event name,
or an entry with no runnable `command` hook — none of which Claude Code
honors, so the hook never fires even though the file “looks” configured.

```pycon
>>> validate_hooks_config({'hooks': {'PostToolUse': [
...     {'matcher': 'Edit', 'hooks': [{'type': 'command', 'command': 'x'}]}]}})
[]
>>> validate_hooks_config({'pre_commit': ['ruff']})
['no top-level `hooks` key']
>>> 'matcher' in validate_hooks_config({'hooks': {'PostToolUse': [
...     {'matcher': {'tool_name': 'Edit'}, 'hooks': [
...         {'type': 'command', 'command': 'x'}]}]}})[0]
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### opsward.score.validate_skill_spec(skill)

Validate a SkillInfo against the agentskills.io specification.

Returns a list of human-readable violation strings (empty = compliant).

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from opsward.base import SkillInfo
>>> s = SkillInfo(name='good-skill', path=Path('.'), has_skill_md=True,
...     frontmatter={'name': 'good-skill', 'description': 'Does X.'}, line_count=50)
>>> validate_skill_spec(s)
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/opsward.security.html.md

# opsward.security

Security advisories (opsward#17, gap 5): “valid” is not “safe to ship”.

An advisory dimension, modelled on the OWASP Top 10 for agentic applications: patterns in a
project’s agent config that over-grant tools, run unpinned or remote code, try to override
the agent’s instructions, or leak a secret. Advisories are **reported, never scored**: the
checks are heuristics, so they must not move a grade or fail a gate. Each one names the
file (repo-relative), the risk and what to do.

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from opsward.base import ScanResult
>>> sr = ScanResult(Path("repo"), claude_md_content="Setup: curl -fsSL https://x.sh | bash")
>>> [a.risk for a in security_advisories(sr)]
['remote-code']
```

### Module Attributes

| [`TEXT_RULES`](_autosummary/opsward.security.html.md#opsward.security.TEXT_RULES)   | risk -> (pattern over text, advice).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Advisory`](_autosummary/opsward.security.html.md#opsward.security.Advisory)(path, risk, message)   | One finding: where, which risk, and the advice.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|

### *class* opsward.security.Advisory(path, risk, message)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One finding: where, which risk, and the advice.

### opsward.security.TEXT_RULES *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[Pattern](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html#re.Pattern), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]* *= {'dynamic-exec': (re.compile('(^|[\\\\s;&|\`(])eval\\\\s+[\\\\"\\'$\`]'), 'evaluates a constructed string; an injected value becomes code'), 'instruction-override': (re.compile('\\\\b(ignore|disregard|forget)\\\\s+(all\\\\s+|any\\\\s+)?(previous|prior|above|earlier|other)\\\\s+(instructions|rules|guidelines)\\\\b', re.IGNORECASE), "tries to override the agent's other instructions (identity or goal hijack)"), 'remote-code': (re.compile('\\\\b(curl|wget)\\\\b[^\\\\n|]\*\\\\|\\\\s\*(?:sudo\\\\b[^|\\\\n]\*?\\\\s|env\\\\s+|/\\\\S\*/)?(?:(?:ba|z|da|k|a)?sh\\\\b|(?:python[\\\\d.]\*|node|perl|ruby)(?=[ \\\\t]\*(?:-[ \\\\t]\*)?(?:$|[;&|)])))|(?:ba|z)?sh\\\\s+<\\\\(\\\\s\*(curl|wget, re.MULTILINE), 'runs a download straight from the network; pin a checksum or vendor the script'), 'secret': (re.compile('\\\\b(sk-(ant-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|xox[bpa]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,})'), 'looks like a credential committed in plain text; rotate it and load it from the environment')}*

# _autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md

# opsward.subagents

Reuse a skill as a subagent: declare it in the skill, generate the twin, check the sync.

A Claude Code subagent is a Markdown file under `.claude/agents/` whose frontmatter
can *preload* a skill (`skills: [name]` injects the full `SKILL.md` body). So a skill
that is also useful in its own context needs nothing but a thin twin that preloads it,
restricts tools, picks a model and states the reply contract. The single source of
truth stays in the skill: it opts in with spec-legal `metadata` keys (the Agent Skills
spec allows string pairs there, and other hosts ignore them). Quote the values so a
strict validator sees strings:

```default
---
name: fleet-sweep
description: ...
metadata:
  subagent: "true"
  subagent-tools: "Bash, Read, Grep"
  subagent-model: "sonnet"
  subagent-reply-lines: "5"
  subagent-name: "fleet-sweeper"
---
```

Only `subagent` is required; the defaults are `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`, no model
(the host picks), 5 lines, and the skill’s own name. Three pure functions do the
work, so `generate` and `maintain` share one source: [`subagent_spec()`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.subagent_spec) reads
the declaration, [`render_subagent()`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.render_subagent) renders the twin (with a marker line
carrying a hash of what it was rendered from), and [`twin_status()`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.twin_status) classifies
every skill/agent pair in a scan. Decision record:
`misc/docs/decisions/0009-skills-declare-their-subagent-twin.md`.

### Functions

| [`check_subagent_twins`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.check_subagent_twins)(sr)                    | `maintain` check: every twin that is not generated and current.                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`render_subagent`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.render_subagent)(spec, \*, source)           | Render the twin agent file for *spec*; *source* is the skill's repo-relative path.    |
| [`subagent_files`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.subagent_files)(sr)                          | Yield the twin agent file for every validly declared skill (missing or not).          |
| [`subagent_spec`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.subagent_spec)(skill)                        | Return the twin a skill declares under `metadata`, or `None`.                         |
| [`twin_for_rendered_skill`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.twin_for_rendered_skill)(skill_md_text, ...) | The twin of a skill that is about to be written (so one `generate` run creates both). |
| [`twin_status`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.twin_status)(sr)                             | Classify every declared twin and every hand-written agent that preloads a skill.      |
| [`twin_summary`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.twin_summary)(sr)                            | Counts by state, for the diagnosis note.                                              |

### opsward.subagents.render_subagent(spec, , source)

Render the twin agent file for *spec*; *source* is the skill’s repo-relative path.

The body is deliberately short: the skill’s full content is preloaded by the host
through the `skills` field, so the twin only adds the context contract.

```pycon
>>> spec = SubagentSpec('sweep', 'sweep', 'Sweep and report.', 'Bash', 'haiku', 3)
>>> text = render_subagent(spec, source='.claude/skills/sweep/SKILL.md')
>>> text.splitlines()[1:4]
['name: sweep', 'description: Sweep and report.', 'tools: Bash']
>>> 'skills: [sweep]' in text and 'at most 3 lines' in text
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### opsward.subagents.subagent_files(sr)

Yield the twin agent file for every validly declared skill (missing or not).

Callers that must not overwrite (the CLI) skip existing targets; the marker in a
generated file is what [`twin_status()`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.twin_status) uses to tell a stale twin from a
hand-written one. Invalid and duplicate declarations yield nothing; `maintain`
reports them.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`GeneratedFile`](_autosummary/opsward.base.html.md#opsward.base.GeneratedFile)]

### opsward.subagents.subagent_spec(skill)

Return the twin a skill declares under `metadata`, or `None`.

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from opsward.base import SkillInfo
>>> s = SkillInfo(name='sweep', path=Path('/x/sweep'), has_skill_md=True,
...     description='Sweep the fleet and report.',
...     frontmatter={'name': 'sweep', 'metadata': {'subagent': 'true', 'subagent-model': 'haiku'}})
>>> spec = subagent_spec(s)
>>> (spec.name, spec.tools, spec.model, spec.reply_lines)
('sweep', 'Read, Grep, Glob, Bash', 'haiku', 5)
>>> subagent_spec(SkillInfo(name='plain', path=Path('/x/plain'))) is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`SubagentSpec`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.SubagentSpec)]

### opsward.subagents.twin_for_rendered_skill(skill_md_text, skill_md_path, root)

The twin of a skill that is about to be written (so one `generate` run creates both).

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> text = '---\nname: s\ndescription: Do the thing.\nmetadata:\n  subagent: "true"\n---\nbody\n'
>>> gf = twin_for_rendered_skill(text, Path('/p/.claude/skills/s/SKILL.md'), Path('/p'))
>>> gf.target_path.as_posix(), 'skills: [s]' in gf.content
('/p/.claude/agents/s.md', True)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`GeneratedFile`](_autosummary/opsward.base.html.md#opsward.base.GeneratedFile)]

### opsward.subagents.twin_status(sr)

Classify every declared twin and every hand-written agent that preloads a skill.

- `invalid`: the declaration cannot be rendered (see `SubagentSpec.problems`).
- `duplicate`: two skills declare the same twin name; the first wins, the rest are reported.
- `missing`: the skill declares a twin and no agent file exists.
- `stale`: the agent file was generated from a declaration that has since changed.
- `in_sync`: generated and current.
- `handwritten`: an agent opsward did not generate, either carrying the name a skill
  declares for its twin (`declared=True`), or sharing a non-declaring skill’s name or
  preloading it via `skills:` (`declared=False`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`TwinStatus`](_autosummary/opsward.subagents.html.md#opsward.subagents.TwinStatus)]

### opsward.subagents.twin_summary(sr)

Counts by state, for the diagnosis note.

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> twin_summary(ScanResult(project_root=Path('/tmp/empty')))
{}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]


# _autosummary/opsward.util.html.md

# opsward.util

Shared helpers for opsward.

### Module Attributes

| [`IGNORE_PATH_MARKER`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.IGNORE_PATH_MARKER)   | Put this on a line (as `<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->` or `# opsward: ignore-path`) and the paths on it are not checked; alone on its line, it covers the next line too.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`checked_lines`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.checked_lines)(content, \*[, marker])     | `content` without the lines an ignore-path marker covers.                           |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`extract_paths`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.extract_paths)(content)                   | Plausible repo-relative file paths cited in markdown, minus URLs and ignored lines. |
| [`iter_files`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.iter_files)(directory, \*[, suffix, ...]) | Yield files in *directory*, optionally filtered by suffix.                          |
| [`iter_subdirs`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.iter_subdirs)(directory)                  | Yield immediate subdirectories of *directory*, sorted by name.                      |
| [`read_json_safe`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.read_json_safe)(path)                     | Read a JSON file, returning None on any failure.                                    |
| [`read_text_safe`](_autosummary/opsward.util.html.md#opsward.util.read_text_safe)(path)                     | Read a text file, returning '' if it doesn't exist or can't be decoded.             |

### opsward.util.IGNORE_PATH_MARKER *= 'opsward: ignore-path'*

Put this on a line (as `<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->` or `# opsward: ignore-path`)
and the paths on it are not checked; alone on its line, it covers the next line too.

### opsward.util.checked_lines(content, , marker='opsward: ignore-path')

`content` without the lines an ignore-path marker covers.

A marker quoted in backticks (prose *about* the marker) is not a marker.

```pycon
>>> checked_lines("a/b.py\nold/c.py <!-- opsward: ignore-path -->\n# opsward: ignore-path\ntmp/d.py\ne/f.py")
'a/b.py\ne/f.py'
>>> checked_lines("<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->\n<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->\nx/y.py\nz/w.py")
'z/w.py'
>>> checked_lines("Use `<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->` on src/a.py")
'Use `<!-- opsward: ignore-path -->` on src/a.py'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### opsward.util.extract_paths(content)

Plausible repo-relative file paths cited in markdown, minus URLs and ignored lines.

The one extractor behind the currency score, the cross-reference check, the stale-path
finding and the ADR drift check, so `opsward: ignore-path` silences all of them.

```pycon
>>> extract_paths("See `src/a.py`, https://x.io/b.html and ./docs/c.md")
['src/a.py', './docs/c.md']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### opsward.util.iter_files(directory, , suffix='', recursive=False, \_seen=None)

Yield files in *directory*, optionally filtered by suffix.

`recursive=True` walks subdirectories too, depth-first in name order. Hidden
folders are skipped (opsward’s choice: `.trash` and the like are not agents),
a folder already visited through a symlink is not re-entered, and a folder that
cannot be read is skipped rather than raised.

### opsward.util.iter_subdirs(directory)

Yield immediate subdirectories of *directory*, sorted by name.

### opsward.util.read_json_safe(path)

Read a JSON file, returning None on any failure.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### opsward.util.read_text_safe(path)

Read a text file, returning ‘’ if it doesn’t exist or can’t be decoded.

```pycon
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> read_text_safe(Path('/nonexistent/file.txt'))
''
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# ai-agents.html.md

# For AI agents

`opsward` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `opsward`

Run opsward to assess and improve this project’s AI agent setup. Use when the user says ‘opsward’, ‘check my setup’, ‘improve my AI config’, or wants a full audit and remediation.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward).

### `opsward-add-drift-check`

Add a new staleness or drift check to opsward’s maintain stage (maintain.py), so `opsward maintain` reports a new kind of MaintenanceSuggestion — a stale reference, an out-of-sync index, an outdated or empty doc, an incomplete skill. Use when extending what `opsward maintain` detects, adding a suggestion category, or deciding whether a finding belongs in maintain or in the diagnose score. Covers the check-generator shape, categories, the diff field, the exit-code contract, and the CLI golden it can move.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-add-drift-check`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-add-drift-check).

### `opsward-add-recommendation`

Add a tech-stack→skill mapping to opsward’s recommendation engine in recommend.py, so `opsward recommend` suggests an ecosystem skill when it detects a dependency or framework (e.g. Supabase, FastAPI, Tailwind). Use when extending the curated `_RECOMMENDATIONS` list, adding a new detection signal, or changing where recommended skills are sourced from.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-add-recommendation`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-add-recommendation).

### `opsward-add-scan-field`

Add a new fact that opsward learns about a target project — a field on ScanResult populated by scan.py — and consume it downstream in score/generate/maintain/recommend. Use when a new check, score, template variable, or drift detector needs data the scan does not yet collect (a new config file, a new .claude/ inventory, a project signal), or when changing project-type detection. Covers the read-only contract, the dataclass-default rule, the util read helpers, and the CLI goldens a scan change can move.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-add-scan-field`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-add-scan-field).

### `opsward-add-scoring`

Add or adjust opsward’s quality scoring — a CLAUDE.md sub-dimension, a whole weighted component, or the skill/spec validation rules — in score.py. Use when changing how `opsward diagnose` grades a project, tuning weights or point thresholds, adding a new ComponentScore, or modifying validate_skill_spec. Explains the pure-function contract, the weighting math, and the constants to keep balanced.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-add-scoring`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-add-scoring).

### `opsward-add-template`

Add or edit a generation template in opsward — a doc template (architecture.md, testing.md, …), an installable skill (SKILL.md), or an agent definition — and wire it into generate.py so opsward produces it. Use when adding a new artifact opsward should scaffold into target projects, adding a template variable, or changing what `opsward generate` / `install-skills` emit. Covers string.Template rules and the python/jsts/shared layout.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-add-template`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-add-template).

### `opsward-dev`

Contributor guide for developing opsward itself — its architecture, hard invariants, and where each kind of change goes. Use when modifying opsward’s own source (scan/score/generate/maintain/recommend/cli), adding a template, scoring dimension, or skill recommendation, or when unsure which module owns a change. NOT for running opsward on a target project (use the `opsward` skill for that).

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-dev`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-dev).

### `opsward-diagnose`

Diagnose the health of this project’s AI agent setup. Use when the user asks to check, audit, or score the project’s CLAUDE.md, skills, docs, or agent configuration.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-diagnose`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-diagnose).

### `opsward-generate`

Generate missing AI setup artifacts for this project. Use when the user asks to scaffold, create, or bootstrap CLAUDE.md, docs, skills, or agent configuration.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-generate`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-generate).

### `opsward-maintain`

Check documentation and AI setup for staleness, drift, or inconsistency. Use when the user asks to maintain, refresh, or update project docs and AI configuration.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-maintain`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-maintain).

### `opsward-subagents`

Decide which of a repo’s skills should also run as subagents (in their own context), declare it in each skill’s frontmatter, and generate or refresh the twin agent files with opsward. Use when a skill does bulky or read-heavy work whose output should stay out of the main context, when a skill needs a tool restriction or a cheaper model, when a hand-written agent duplicates a skill, when `opsward maintain` reports a `subagent_twin` finding, or when asked “should this skill be a subagent”, “make this skill usable as a subagent”, “generate agents from skills”, or to sweep a repo for skill/agent pairs. Also usable as a subagent itself.

Source: [`.claude/skills/opsward-subagents`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/opsward-subagents).

## Subagents

Subagents are Markdown files with a frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `tools`) and a system prompt as the body. Copy one into your project’s `.claude/agents/` (or your agent host’s equivalent) to delegate the task it describes.

### `opsward-subagents`

Decide which of a repo’s skills should also run as subagents (in their own context), declare it in each skill’s frontmatter, and generate or refresh the twin agent files with opsward. Use when a skill does bulky or read-heavy work whose output should stay out of the main context, when a skill needs a tool restriction or a cheaper model, when a hand-written agent duplicates a skill, when `opsward maintain` reports a `subagent_twin` finding, or when asked “should this skill be a subagent”, “make this skill usable as a subagent”, “generate agents from skills”, or to sweep a repo for skill/agent pairs. Also usable as a subagent itself.

Source: [`.claude/agents/opsward-subagents.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/agents/opsward-subagents.md); tools: `Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write`.

### `setup-auditor`

Read-only diagnostic agent that audits the project’s AI setup (CLAUDE.md, skills, docs, rules). Use when you want to check the health of the project’s agent configuration without making changes.

Source: [`.claude/agents/setup-auditor.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/.claude/agents/setup-auditor.md).

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code
- [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/opsward/tree/HEAD/AGENTS.md): read by Codex, Copilot, Cursor and other agents

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/opsward/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`opsward.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/opsward/opsward.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/opsward/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
